findings.summary: Ferrule achieves higher mean test AUROC than Arbor-GBT on all six datasets in the suite, with differences ranging from 0.7 to 1.2 percentage points.
findings.scope: Six binary-classification datasets (2,400–310,000 rows), test AUROC (×100), mean over 5 seeds, fixed 70/10/20 split, 50-trial hyperparameter search.
findings.caveats: No statistical tests were reported, so the consistency of the advantage across datasets cannot be formally assessed; the differences are small (≤1.2 points).

findings.summary: Ferrule also outperforms logistic regression on all six datasets, with larger margins (3.6–4.4 percentage points) than against Arbor-GBT.
findings.scope: Same six datasets and evaluation conditions as F1.
findings.caveats: No statistical tests reported; logistic regression is a simple reference, not a tuned competitor.

findings.summary: The evidence supports that Ferrule outperforms Arbor-GBT on this specific suite, but the absence of statistical tests means the result cannot be claimed as statistically significant or reliable beyond the observed means.
findings.scope: All six datasets in the suite; test AUROC means.

drafts.passage: Ferrule achieved higher mean test AUROC than Arbor-GBT on all six datasets in the suite, with margins ranging from 0.7 to 1.2 percentage points (e.g., 93.7 vs. 92.8 on Ivel-Fraud and 76.4 vs. 75.6 on Pemberly-Claims). Ferrule also outperformed logistic regression on all six datasets, with larger margins of 3.6–4.4 percentage points. These results support that Ferrule outperforms Arbor-GBT on this specific suite, but because no statistical tests were reported, the advantage cannot be claimed as statistically significant or reliable beyond the observed means.
